PYQ-POL-WEB-45ADDD.lead: Ambedkar called Article 32, the Right to Constitutional Remedies, the heart and soul.

The Right to Property was removed from Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment (1978).
PYQ-POL-WEB-45ADDD.also: The Supreme Court treats Article 32 as part of the basic structure.

PYQ-POL-WEB-52223D.lead: Members were indirectly elected by the provincial legislative assemblies.

PYQ-POL-WEB-E283C4.also: Ivor Jennings called it 'too long and too rigid'.

Rajendra Prasad was elected first President of India the same day.

PYQ-POL-WEB-F06B7A.lead: Mahatma Gandhi was never a member of the Constituent Assembly or its Drafting Committee.

A presidential system gives more stability but checks responsibility only periodically.

PYQ-POL-4ADE4E1D118F.lead: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 came into force on 1 July 1961.
points: 20 May 1961 is the date of Presidential assent, not commencement.
1 June and 20 June 1961 are wrong dates.
It makes giving, taking or demanding dowry an offence.
Section 498A IPC (cruelty, 1983) and 304B IPC (dowry death, 1986) were added later.

PYQ-POL-4BB919732E3C.lead: Article 32 empowers the Supreme Court to issue writs.
points: High Courts under Article 226 can issue writs for FRs and 'any other purpose', so their writ power is wider.

PYQ-POL-4CF5E9089C42.lead: Article 20(2) gives protection against double jeopardy.
points: It applies only when a person was prosecuted and punished by a court for the same offence.
It does not apply to departmental or administrative proceedings.
The other three options are not legal terms for this protection.
PYQ-POL-4CF5E9089C42.also: Article 20(1) bars ex-post-facto criminal laws; 20(3) bars self-incrimination.

PYQ-POL-4D8A1F42157D.lead: Article 19 freedoms are available only to citizens.
points: Other citizen-only rights: Articles 15, 16, 29 and 30.
Correct code A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV is option 2.
PYQ-POL-4E2815A3CF9D.also: Article 18 exempts military and academic distinctions.

PYQ-POL-4F44363EBDEF.lead: Section 377 IPC criminalised consensual same-sex acts — an LGBT rights issue.
points: Suresh Kumar Koushal (2013) had upheld Section 377.
In 2016 the curative petitions were referred to a five-judge Bench.
Navtej Singh Johar (2018) decriminalised consensual adult same-sex conduct.
Free legal aid was read into Article 21 in M.H. Hoskot (1978) and Hussainara Khatoon (1979).
Article 22 (V) is the distractor: it gives right to consult a lawyer of choice on arrest.
PYQ-POL-5031979CD36B.also: Article 39A (42nd Amendment) directs the State to provide free legal aid.

PYQ-POL-50E26166E9DB.lead: Freedom of speech (Article 19(1)(a)) is for citizens only.
points: Articles 15 and 16 in the equality group are citizen-only, but Article 14 covers everyone.

PYQ-POL-52C20F13D4FF.lead: Article 16(4A) is about SC/ST reservation in promotions.
points: The 85th Amendment, 2001 added consequential seniority.
M. Nagaraj (2006) upheld these amendments with conditions.

PYQ-POL-53D2661F2CCE.lead: Article 20(1) bars retrospective criminal laws, so statement 2 is wrong.

head: No.
Claim (short)
True/False — why
rows: Parliament can make retrospective criminal law
No compulsion to be witness against self
Art 22 safeguards not for preventive detainees

points: Civil and tax laws can be retrospective; only criminal laws cannot.

PYQ-POL-557A42B74133.lead: Foreigners get Article 14 equality and Article 21 life and liberty.
points: Foreigners also get Articles 20, 22 (not enemy aliens), 23-24 and 25-28.

PYQ-POL-578614405D30.lead: Code a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i matches first chairpersons.
points: NCSC and NCST became separate bodies after the 89th Amendment, 2003.
NCBC got constitutional status under Article 338B by the 102nd Amendment, 2018.

PYQ-POL-591B828C49BC.lead: Under Article 32 a person goes directly to the Supreme Court: original jurisdiction.
points: Unlike Article 131, the Article 32 remedy is itself a Fundamental Right.

PYQ-POL-5CD185446D85.lead: Article 34 is about martial law, not SC economic safeguards.

head: No.
Article
Subject
rows: Promote economic, educational interests of SC/ST
Ban on forced labour and begar

points: Articles 23, 24 and 46 are listed as economic safeguards for Scheduled Castes.

PYQ-POL-5D10D5888283.lead: Article 12 does not mention courts, so their status as 'State' is unclear.
points: Courts acting judicially are not 'State' (Naresh Shridhar Mirajkar, 1966).
Their administrative or rule-making acts can be tested against Part III.
Municipal corporations and panchayats are clearly 'local authorities'.

PYQ-POL-602F300F9B4D.lead: The 1995 Act reserved at least 3% of vacancies for persons with disabilities.
points: Section 33: 1% each for blindness/low vision, hearing impairment and locomotor disability.
Reservation was computed on total vacancies in a cadre (Union of India v. National Federation of the Blind, 2013).
The 2016 RPwD Act raised it to 4%.

PYQ-POL-625DA8B76F85.lead: Article 23 bans begar and forced labour, which covers bonded labour.

head: No.
Article
Subject
rows: Ban on begar, forced labour, trafficking
Ban on child labour in factories/mines

points: The exact definition of 'bonded labour' is in the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976, made to enforce Article 23.
PYQ-POL-625DA8B76F85.also: Articles 23 and 24 together form the Right against Exploitation.

PYQ-POL-6315A0E8AFC1.lead: Quo warranto asks a person by what authority he holds a public office.

head: No.
Purpose
Writ
rows: Question right to hold public office

points: Quo warranto lies only for a substantive public office created by statute or Constitution.
Any person can seek it, not only an aggrieved person.

PYQ-POL-637427A1131A.lead: Certiorari makes a lower court send its case records to a higher court.

head: No.
Purpose
Writ
rows: Move case between any two courts

points: The higher court then quashes the order if passed without jurisdiction or with an error of law.
Certiorari is curative (after the order); prohibition is preventive (before it).

PYQ-POL-65736CB2BA39.lead: Only B and C state the standard textbook rules on writs.

head: Stmt
Claim (short)
True/False — why
rows: Habeas corpus only against public authorities

points: So the answer is B and C only.
PYQ-POL-65736CB2BA39.also: Mandamus also cannot be issued against the President or State Governors.

PYQ-POL-65EED9CE550B.lead: Habeas corpus orders the detained person's body to be produced before court.
points: Habeas corpus means 'to have the body'.
It can be issued against both public authorities and private persons.

PYQ-POL-6675D5C10A80.lead: The Constitution neither defines basic structure nor expressly mentions 'judicial review'.

head: Stmt
Claim (short)
True/False — why
rows: False — doctrine made by Supreme Court
False — not expressly stated; implied power

points: Basic structure came from Kesavananda Bharati (1973); its parts are listed by courts case by case.
Judicial review flows from Articles 13, 32 and 226, but the term is not in the text.
PYQ-POL-6675D5C10A80.also: Judicial review itself is part of the basic structure (Minerva Mills 1980, L. Chandra Kumar 1997).

PYQ-POL-66B995530AFB.lead: Article 300A makes property a legal right available to every person.

head: No.
Option
Why right/wrong
rows: Wrong — removed from Part III in 1978
Wrong — it is a constitutional/legal right

points: The 44th Amendment, 1978 omitted Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 and inserted Article 300A in Part XII.
For its violation, one goes to the High Court under Article 226, not Article 32.

PYQ-POL-66C7102B892D.lead: Article 20 protects against ex post facto laws, double jeopardy and self-incrimination.
points: Art 20(1): no retrospective criminal law; 20(2): no double punishment; 20(3): no self-incrimination.
PYQ-POL-66C7102B892D.also: Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency (44th Amendment).

PYQ-POL-672CA7F1D7E2.lead: Laws in the Ninth Schedule were shielded from challenge on Fundamental Rights.
points: The 76th Amendment Act, 1994 put Tamil Nadu's 69% reservation law in the Ninth Schedule.
Ninth Schedule was added by the 1st Amendment, 1951 (Article 31B).
PYQ-POL-672CA7F1D7E2.also: I.R. Coelho (2007): laws added after 24 April 1973 can be reviewed for basic structure.

PYQ-POL-6A5483A2C9C6.lead: Article 18 allows only military or academic distinctions to be conferred.
points: Article 18(1): 'No title, not being a military or academic distinction, shall be conferred by the State.'
Royal and hereditary titles are exactly what Article 18 abolishes, so options 3 and 4 are wrong.
There is no 'constitutional title' exception (option 1).
PYQ-POL-6A5483A2C9C6.also: Balaji Raghavan (1995): Bharat Ratna and Padma awards are not titles, but cannot be used as prefixes/suffixes.

PYQ-POL-6C7609D2C14F.lead: Article 24 bans employing children below 14 in factories, mines, hazardous work.
PYQ-POL-6C7609D2C14F.also: Articles 23 and 24 form the Right against Exploitation.

PYQ-POL-6F5D85D4F73A.lead: Not punishing twice for one offence is the doctrine of double jeopardy.
points: Article 20(2) protects only after prosecution and punishment by a court; departmental action does not count (Maqbool Hussain, 1953).

PYQ-POL-76E6F1F61DC1.lead: The Court upheld criminal defamation, IPC Sections 499 and 500.
points: Subramanian Swamy v. Union of India was decided in May 2016.
Defamation is an express ground of restriction in Article 19(2).
The Court treated reputation as part of the right to life under Article 21.
Sedition, blasphemy and obscenity were not the provisions in issue.

PYQ-POL-77C9941B15EC.lead: Part III order: Equality, Freedom, Religion, Cultural-Educational, Constitutional Remedies.
points: Right against Exploitation (23–24) comes between Freedom and Religion but is not listed here.
So the sequence is D, C, B, E, A — option 2.

PYQ-POL-7A33BDAF645D.lead: Mandamus commands a public authority to perform its public duty.
points: Mandamus means 'we command'.
It does not lie against a private individual or private body (options 3, 4), except where a public duty is involved.
It can also go to lower courts, but the standard answer is public authority.
PYQ-POL-7A33BDAF645D.also: Mandamus cannot be issued against the President or State Governors.

PYQ-POL-7AADD9E03E00.lead: Privacy is part of life and personal liberty under Article 21.

head: No.
Article
Subject
rows: No discrimination on religion, caste, sex etc.
Life and personal liberty incl. privacy

points: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (24 August 2017): nine-judge bench, unanimous.
It overruled M.P. Sharma (1954) and Kharak Singh (1962) on this point.
PYQ-POL-7AADD9E03E00.also: Privacy is not absolute; limits must pass legality, legitimate aim and proportionality.

PYQ-POL-7C5FA5C4A067.lead: A.K. Gopalan (1950) read 'procedure established by law' narrowly.
points: Gopalan held any procedure in a valid law is enough; no American 'due process'.
Maneka Gandhi (1978) changed this: procedure must be fair, just and reasonable.

PYQ-POL-7CAB9C8D5D22.lead: The Right to Education Act was passed in 2009.
points: Full name: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009.
It came into force on 1 April 2010 — option 4 is the commencement year, not passing year.
It gives effect to Article 21A (children aged 6 to 14).
PYQ-POL-7CAB9C8D5D22.also: Article 21A was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

PYQ-POL-7CB608E7C4E9.lead: Quo warranto literally means 'by what authority' or 'by what warrant'.
points: The court asks the office holder to show the legal authority for holding a public office.
Options 2–4 describe kinds of authority, not the meaning of the words.
PYQ-POL-7CB608E7C4E9.also: Quo warranto lies only for a substantive public office, not a private or ministerial post.

PYQ-POL-7CC62124D2A3.lead: Free and compulsory education (6–14 years) is a Fundamental Right, Article 21A.

head: No.
Option
Status
rows: Enabling provision Art 16(4A), not a right
Art 24 — only factories, mines, hazardous work
Part of Art 19(1)(a) by court ruling

points: Article 21A was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002; the RTE Act followed in 2009.

PYQ-POL-803B19401388.lead: Gujarat was the first State to implement 10% EWS reservation, January 2019.
points: Gujarat applied the EWS quota from 14 January 2019, the day the central rule came into force.
The quota comes from the 103rd Amendment Act, 2019 (Articles 15(6) and 16(6)).

PYQ-POL-8230CB1C5972.lead: The 103rd Amendment allows up to 10% reservation for economically weaker sections.
points: Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (7 November 2022) upheld it by a 3:2 majority.
The quota covers education (Article 15(6)) and public jobs (Article 16(6)).
The Court held economic criteria alone can be a basis for reservation.
PYQ-POL-8230CB1C5972.also: EWS quota excludes SC, ST and OBC, and is over and above existing reservations.

PYQ-POL-82ACA523DBB8.lead: Freedom of Religion is in Articles 25 to 28.
points: Art 25: conscience and religion; 26: manage religious affairs; 27: no tax for a religion; 28: religious instruction in institutions.

PYQ-POL-865AF9CCE260.lead: Article 32 lets a person move the Supreme Court directly to enforce Fundamental Rights.

head: No.
Article
Subject
rows: Parliament may limit FRs of armed forces

points: Ambedkar called Article 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

PYQ-POL-875B90704E4F.lead: Mandamus is Latin for 'we command' — an order to perform a public duty.

head: No.
Word
Linked to
rows: A ground for review, not a meaning

PYQ-POL-8AC08B562241.lead: After RTE, the Centre brought the National Food Security (Right to Food) Bill.
points: The National Food Security Bill was introduced in Lok Sabha in December 2011.
It became the National Food Security Act, 2013.
No central Right to Health or Right to Shelter Act was introduced then.

PYQ-POL-8AC23F763FF4.lead: Article 12 defines 'the State' for Part III.
points: It includes Union and State governments and legislatures, and all local or other authorities.
PYQ-POL-8AC23F763FF4.also: Courts treat bodies that are instrumentalities of government as 'other authorities' (Ajay Hasia, 1981).

PYQ-POL-8B4A831221B2.lead: Right to Property is no longer a Fundamental Right since 1978.
points: The 44th Amendment, 1978 removed Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 and added Article 300A.

PYQ-POL-8C7C3EB46579.lead: Article 14 forbids class legislation but allows reasonable classification.
points: Class legislation means arbitrarily picking a group for special favour or burden.
Classification is valid if it has an intelligible differentia and a rational link to the law's object.
Protective and differential laws (e.g., for women, children, backward classes) are allowed if they pass this test.

PYQ-POL-8DB488C52D02.lead: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 came into force on 1 July 1961.
points: It was passed on 20 May 1961 (assent date), which is option 1 — a common trap.
It applies to the whole of India.
PYQ-POL-8DB488C52D02.also: Section 498A IPC (cruelty) and 304B IPC (dowry death) were added in 1983 and 1986.

PYQ-POL-9106AE56F56D.lead: Article 12's wide wording plus many court rulings make 'State' hard to pin down.
points: The definition is inclusive ('includes'), and 'other authorities' is not defined.
Courts have widened it case by case (Rajasthan SEB 1967, Ajay Hasia 1981, Pradeep Kumar Biswas 2002).
Whether a body is State often depends on government control and funding, a policy-type judgement.

PYQ-POL-92E39634C4DF.lead: Double jeopardy is in Article 20(2), part of the Right to Freedom (19–22).

PYQ-POL-946A6A8050FA.lead: Article 19(1) now guarantees six freedoms to citizens.
points: They are: speech, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession/trade.
Originally seven; property (19(1)(f)) was omitted by the 44th Amendment, 1978.
Each freedom is subject to reasonable restrictions under clauses (2) to (6).
PYQ-POL-946A6A8050FA.also: Article 19 rights are available only to citizens, not foreigners.

PYQ-POL-95E6B449F9B7.lead: Habeas corpus lies against private persons too, so statement 3 is false.

head: No.
Statement
Correct?
rows: Not if detention outside court's jurisdiction

points: Habeas corpus is also refused where detention is by a court order or for contempt of court/legislature.

PYQ-POL-95F0CB851860.lead: Begar means forced work taken without any payment.
points: Article 23(1) bans begar, human trafficking and other forced labour.
Voluntary unpaid work (option 1) is not begar, since there is no force.
Paying below minimum wage can be 'forced labour' (PUDR, 1982), but that is not begar.
PYQ-POL-95F0CB851860.also: Article 23(2) allows compulsory public service, like military service, without discrimination.

PYQ-POL-969C87171A34.lead: Article 32 is the Right to Constitutional Remedies.
points: It lets a person go straight to the Supreme Court, which can issue the five writs.
PYQ-POL-969C87171A34.also: Ambedkar called Article 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

PYQ-POL-96A3ADFBE4E6.lead: Article 16(3) lets Parliament prescribe residence for certain public jobs.

head: No.
Article
Subject
rows: No tax to promote a religion

points: Article 16(2) bans job discrimination on residence; 16(3) is the exception.
Only Parliament, not State legislatures, can make this law (Article 35).
PYQ-POL-96A3ADFBE4E6.also: Parliament used it in the Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act, 1957.

PYQ-POL-97244FD83A3D.lead: The Central Government notifies minorities under the NCM Act, 1992.
points: The Constitution uses 'minority' (Articles 29, 30) but does not define it.
Section 2(c) of the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992 lets the Centre notify minority communities.
Six are notified: Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains.
PYQ-POL-97244FD83A3D.also: Jains were added as a notified minority in 2014.

PYQ-POL-97612B70243E.lead: Both are right: no unqualified right to marry; travel abroad is within Article 21.

head: Stmt
Claim (short)
True/False — why
rows: Travel abroad is a Fundamental Right

points: Choice of partner is still protected under Article 21 (Shafin Jahan, 2018); A means no right to State-recognised marriage.

PYQ-POL-981259F90754.lead: Article 13(2) bars the State from making laws that abridge Fundamental Rights.
points: Any law breaking this is void to the extent of the conflict.
Article 13 has only four clauses, so 13(5) and 13(7) do not exist.
Article 13(4), added by the 24th Amendment (1971), excludes constitutional amendments from Article 13.
PYQ-POL-981259F90754.also: Article 13(1) covers pre-Constitution laws and is the basis of the doctrine of eclipse.

PYQ-POL-988E531C62A2.lead: Article 20(2) bars prosecuting and punishing anyone twice for one offence.

head: No.
Article
Deals with
rows: Double jeopardy, ex post facto, self-incrimination

points: Protection applies only after prosecution and punishment by a court or judicial tribunal.
It does not bar departmental or administrative proceedings for the same act.
PYQ-POL-988E531C62A2.also: Article 20 has three parts: 20(1) ex post facto, 20(2) double jeopardy, 20(3) self-incrimination.

PYQ-POL-98966D9E30B3.lead: Article 13(2) forbids laws that take away or abridge Part III rights.
points: Exact words: the State shall not make any law which 'takes away or abridges' the rights in Part III.
Option 1 (abridges) is also part of the text; 'takes away' is the first verb used.
Part IV holds Directive Principles; Article 13 does not protect them.
A law violating this is void to the extent of the conflict.
PYQ-POL-98966D9E30B3.also: Article 13(4), added by the 24th Amendment (1971), excludes constitutional amendments from 'law' under Article 13.

PYQ-POL-9949445CFC8B.lead: Article 21A gives free and compulsory education to children aged 6–14.
points: 21A was inserted by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.
The RTE Act, 2009 gives effect to it; both came into force on 1 April 2010.
Earlier, courts read education into Article 21 (Mohini Jain 1992, Unni Krishnan 1993).
PYQ-POL-9949445CFC8B.also: The same 86th Amendment changed Article 45 (DPSP) and added duty 51A(k) for parents.

PYQ-POL-9B2341745553.lead: Most rights bind the State, but some also bind private individuals.
points: Articles 15(2), 17, 23 and 24 can be enforced against private persons too.
So rights can be claimed against both the State and private individuals.
Option 3 (only State) misses these rights; options 1 and 4 ignore the State.
Most Part III rights, like Article 14 or 19, apply only against the 'State' under Article 12.
PYQ-POL-9B2341745553.also: Article 12 defines 'State' to include Union, States, local and other authorities.

PYQ-POL-9BABB167A5F8.lead: The 44th Amendment, 1978 removed property from the Fundamental Rights.
points: The amendment omitted Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31.
Property is now a constitutional (legal) right under Article 300A in Part XII.

PYQ-POL-9C662F5674C8.lead: The Supreme Court held choice of life partner is part of Article 21.
points: Shafin Jahan v. Asokan K.M. (Hadiya case, 2018) linked marriage choice to Article 21.
Shakti Vahini v. Union of India (2018) protected couples from khap panchayat threats.
PYQ-POL-9C662F5674C8.also: Supriyo Chakraborty (2023) said there is no unqualified fundamental right to marry as an institution.

PYQ-POL-9D42C1CB0887.lead: High Courts issue writs under Article 226.

head: No.
Article
Deals with
rows: Parliament's power on certain Part III laws
HC withdraws case from lower court

points: Article 226 covers Fundamental Rights 'and for any other purpose', so it is wider than Article 32.
Article 32 is limited to enforcing Fundamental Rights.
PYQ-POL-9D42C1CB0887.also: Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right; Article 226 is not.

PYQ-POL-9DF21ADDBAFB.lead: Under Article 32, a person can directly approach the Supreme Court.
points: No need to go to a High Court first for a Fundamental Rights violation.
Article 131 is also original jurisdiction, but only for federal disputes.
PYQ-POL-9DF21ADDBAFB.also: Ambedkar called Article 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

PYQ-POL-A1BEDB62082E.lead: The 44th Amendment, 1978 deleted the right to property from Part III.
points: It omitted Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31, effective 20 June 1979.
Property became a legal right under the new Article 300A.
Right to Freedom and Right to Equality still remain Fundamental Rights.
Right to Education was added, not removed, by the 86th Amendment, 2002.
PYQ-POL-A1BEDB62082E.also: The 44th Amendment also said Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended during an Emergency.

PYQ-POL-A22F2BB410B6.lead: Ex post facto law means a law that acts retrospectively.
points: It applies to acts done before the law was made.
Article 20(1) bars retrospective criminal laws and higher punishment than at the time of the act.
Retrospective civil and tax laws are not barred by Article 20(1).
Earlier, present and future law do not describe this backward effect.

PYQ-POL-A3C464F8CBC6.lead: K.A. Najeeb (2021) linked bail after long undertrial custody to Article 21.
points: A three-judge Bench upheld bail for an accused jailed over five years under UAPA without trial.
The Court said Section 43-D(5) UAPA cannot override the right to speedy trial under Article 21.
Articles 14, 16 and 19 (equality, public jobs, freedoms) were not the basis.
PYQ-POL-A3C464F8CBC6.also: Speedy trial was first read into Article 21 in Hussainara Khatoon (1979).

PYQ-POL-A4CD0991F7E0.lead: Legislatures, not the Supreme Court, impose limits on Fundamental Rights.
points: The question asks for the incorrect statement, so statement 1 is the answer.
Courts only test whether restrictions made by law are reasonable.

PYQ-POL-A7629A72C272.lead: An ex post facto law, by definition, operates retrospectively.
points: It reaches back to acts done before the law was passed.
Article 20(1) forbids such laws only for creating crimes or raising penalties.
Prospective or future laws apply only from now on — the opposite idea.
A proposed Bill is not yet a law at all.

PYQ-POL-A792422D688A.lead: The Court treated maternity benefit as part of the right to life (Article 21).
points: K. Umadevi v. Government of Tamil Nadu (2025) linked maternity benefit to reproductive rights and dignity.
Her two earlier children were born before she joined service, from a first marriage.
Articles 14, 23 and 21A deal with equality, exploitation and education — not the main basis.
PYQ-POL-A792422D688A.also: Reproductive choice was earlier read into Article 21 in Suchita Srivastava (2009).

PYQ-POL-A9151258E624.lead: Each writ's Latin name gives its meaning.
points: So the correct code is option 2 (a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i).
Option 1 repeats 'iv' for two items, so it cannot be right.
PYQ-POL-A9151258E624.also: Prohibition means 'to forbid'; it is issued before a lower court decides.

PYQ-POL-A984908A3FA4.lead: Article 33 lets Parliament restrict Fundamental Rights of the armed forces.
points: It covers armed forces, paramilitary, police, intelligence bodies and similar.
Only Parliament, not State legislatures, can make such laws.
PYQ-POL-A984908A3FA4.also: Article 34 restricts rights while martial law is in force.

PYQ-POL-AABBDB75971B.lead: Article 15(3) allows special provisions for women and children.

head: No.
Clause
Provides
rows: Special provisions for SEBC, SC, ST

points: 15(4) was added by the 1st Amendment, 1951; 15(5) by the 93rd Amendment, 2005.
PYQ-POL-AABBDB75971B.also: 15(6), added by the 103rd Amendment (2019), enables EWS provisions.

PYQ-POL-AC92B26EA0EF.lead: Articles 14 to 18 form the Right to Equality.
points: 14 equality before law; 15 no discrimination; 16 equal job opportunity; 17 untouchability; 18 titles.
PYQ-POL-AC92B26EA0EF.also: Six groups start at Articles 14, 19, 23, 25, 29 and 32.

PYQ-POL-AC9E5D3B17F3.lead: Article 24 bans employing children below 14 in factories, mines, hazardous work.
points: The Child Labour Act, 1986 (amended 2016) gives it legal force.

PYQ-POL-AD208C7C6B4D.lead: Press freedom is part of free speech under Article 19(1)(a).
points: The Constitution does not mention the press separately.
Romesh Thappar (1950) and Indian Express (1985) read it into 19(1)(a).
It is subject to reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2).

PYQ-POL-APK-04B6F0.lead: Article 14 guarantees equality before law and equal protection of laws.
points: It applies to 'any person', citizens and foreigners alike.
PYQ-POL-APK-04B6F0.also: 'Equality before law' is from Britain; 'equal protection of laws' from the USA.

PYQ-POL-APK-158179.lead: Mandamus ('we command') orders an authority to do its legal duty.

head: No.
Writ

The options are Schedules of the AP Reorganisation Act, not of the Constitution.

PYQ-POL-WEB-BF6AAD.lead: Part VIII (Sections 76–83) of the Act covers provisions as to services.
points: It covers All-India Services and the division of State government employees.
Part VI covers apportionment of assets and liabilities.
Part IV covers the High Court.

PYQ-POL-WEB-C52BD8.lead: Provinces could opt out; Assembly members were to be elected, not nominated.
points: Only the Princely States' representatives were to be nominated by their rulers.
Cripps Mission came in March 1942; Gandhi called it a 'post-dated cheque'.

PYQ-POL-WEB-D42A10.lead: Section 84 creates the Apex Council for Godavari and Krishna waters.
points: Section 85 then sets up the two River Management Boards.
Section 20 is duration of Legislative Assemblies; the ST Order amendment is Section 29.
Section 16 is about sitting members; Section 25 is about Council Chairman and Deputy Chairman.

PYQ-POL-WEB-D4F306.lead: Art 239(2): such a Governor acts independently of his Council of Ministers.
points: A State's ministers have no say over a UT, which the Union runs.
Option 4 is wrong: Art 239(2) expressly allows such an appointment.
Example: the Punjab Governor is also the Administrator of Chandigarh.

PYQ-POL-WEB-ED2D09.lead: Only statement 1 is correct; the Constitution did not adopt linguistic States.

False — no such recommendation or provision

points: Gandhi supported linguistic provinces since the Congress Nagpur session, 1920.
The Dhar Commission (1948) and the JVP Committee (1949) advised against immediate linguistic reorganisation.
Andhra State (1953) was the first linguistic State; the States Reorganisation Act followed in 1956.

PYQ-POL-275F0A31C351.lead: Part II, Articles 5–11, deals with Citizenship.

PYQ-POL-44E710B5DC5D.lead: Articles 5 to 8 decide who became a citizen at the commencement.
points: Option 1 is the best fit; the full citizenship Part runs Articles 5–11.
Option 2 leaves out Article 5, the main provision.
Articles 3 and 4 deal with new States, not citizenship.

PYQ-POL-56F9A54A835B.lead: Article 10 continues citizenship, subject to laws made by Parliament.

Subject

PYQ-POL-5A8AE8A68A86.lead: Article 11 lets Parliament regulate citizenship by law.
points: Parliament used Article 11 to pass the Citizenship Act, 1955.

PYQ-POL-704E44D47A56.lead: Article 6 covers people who migrated to India from Pakistan.
points: Bangladesh did not exist in 1950; it was East Pakistan.
Sri Lanka and Nepal are not covered by Article 6.
Article 7 covers the reverse: people who migrated to Pakistan.

PYQ-POL-82DB13A71659.lead: After 19 July 1948, migrants had to be registered by a Dominion officer.
points: Article 6(b)(ii) also required six months' residence in India before applying.
Birth in India (self, parent or grandparent) applied to all migrants, so it did not separate late arrivals.
No oath or Pakistani residence test was required.

PYQ-POL-8B878D2E5477.lead: Article 5 sets out citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.
points: Article 5 needs domicile plus birth in India, a parent born in India, or five years' residence.

PYQ-POL-8BF9CAA5DB01.lead: Article 11 lets Parliament legislate on acquiring and ending citizenship.
points: The Citizenship Act, 1955 was made under Article 11.

PYQ-POL-8F58C6DB9EF8.lead: Article 9: voluntarily taking foreign citizenship ends Indian citizenship.
points: After 1950, the same rule is in Section 9 of the Citizenship Act, 1955.

PYQ-POL-950B3E4711EC.lead: Indian citizenship is never based on ethnic identity.
points: The Citizenship Act, 1955 gives five modes: birth, descent, registration, naturalisation, incorporation of territory.
Birth, registration and naturalisation are all valid modes.

PYQ-POL-971940216D36.lead: E-governance, energy management and urban mobility are Smart Solutions; B is not.
points: Other Smart Solutions include waste management and water management.
Smart Cities Mission was launched in June 2015.

PYQ-POL-A9F1C4FBD5C9.lead: An Indian passport was never a condition under Article 5.
points: Article 5 needs domicile in India plus one of three: birth in India, a parent born in India, or five years' residence.
Domicile is compulsory; birth and parent's birth are alternative conditions in the list.

PYQ-POL-APK-007407.lead: Article 51A(g) is the duty to protect and improve the natural environment.
points: The matching Directive Principle is Article 48A, the State's duty on environment.

PYQ-POL-APK-1CDE44.lead: 10 continues rights, 8 covers Indians abroad, 9 foreign citizenship, 5 commencement.
points: This gives A-2, B-4, C-1, D-3, which is option 1.

PYQ-POL-APK-1D4C27.lead: The 42nd Amendment, 1976 added Fundamental Duties as Part IVA.
points: It added ten duties in Article 51A, on the Swaran Singh Committee's advice.
The 86th Amendment, 2002 added the eleventh duty on education of children.
The 44th Amendment (1978) reversed many 42nd changes but kept the duties.

PYQ-POL-APK-281481.lead: Livelihood and equal pay are socialistic (economic-social) principles under Article 39.

head: Stmt
Principle

rows: Equal pay for equal work — Art 39(d)

PYQ-POL-APK-2B54AA.lead: Swaran Singh Committee (1976) suggested eight Fundamental Duties.
points: The Government accepted the idea but added ten duties through the 42nd Amendment.
Committee proposals like penalties for non-compliance were not accepted.

PYQ-POL-APK-2F45BB.lead: Owning land or property never gives Indian citizenship.
points: Valid modes: birth, descent, registration, naturalisation and incorporation of territory (Citizenship Act, 1955).
Options 1–3 are all legal modes of acquiring citizenship.

PYQ-POL-APK-48E61B.lead: CAA helps persecuted minorities; persecution is the reason for the law.
points: It covers Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis and Christians from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan.
They must have entered India on or before 31 December 2014.
Their naturalisation residence period was cut from 11 years to 5 years.

PYQ-POL-APK-6A9E2E.lead: Part II, Articles 5–11, deals with citizenship.

PYQ-POL-APK-6C69AC.lead: Democracy brings people's participation and makes government answerable.
points: Accountable rulers tend to respond to people's needs, aiding development.
Options 1, 3 and 4 describe the opposite of democracy.

PYQ-POL-APK-72CBEE.lead: A Citizen's Charter promises service standards, timelines and grievance redress.
points: India adopted Citizen's Charters in 1997, inspired by the UK's 1991 scheme.
Investment, defence spending and population are not its purpose.

PYQ-POL-APK-88481B.lead: The Citizenship Act was amended in 2003, 2015 and 2019, but not in 2008.
points: 2003 amendment brought in Overseas Citizenship and the 'illegal migrant' concept.
2015 merged PIO into OCI; 2019 was the CAA.

PYQ-POL-APK-89AAF0.lead: Technology in e-governance improves service delivery and citizen engagement.
points: It brings online services, faster delivery and transparency.
It supports, not replaces, human interaction; cost cutting is a side benefit, not the core role.

PYQ-POL-APK-8B650A.lead: Depositing money in a bank is not a mode of citizenship.
points: 'Neutralization' means naturalisation; 'convention of a territory' means incorporation of territory.
Birth, naturalisation and incorporation are all modes under the Citizenship Act, 1955.

PYQ-POL-APK-9B9FAE.lead: Article 11 lets Parliament change citizenship law by ordinary simple majority.
points: Article 11 empowers Parliament to make laws on acquisition and termination of citizenship.
Such laws are not amendments under Article 368, so a simple majority is enough.
Special majority is needed for Article 368 amendments.
Effective and absolute majority are used for other purposes, e.g. removing the Vice-President or Speaker.
PYQ-POL-APK-9B9FAE.also: Other simple-majority changes outside Article 368: new States (Arts 2-4), Fifth and Sixth Schedules, quorum in Parliament.

PYQ-POL-APK-A8689A.lead: India has single citizenship; the law ends Indian citizenship on taking another.
points: The Constitution and the Citizenship Act, 1955 recognise only Indian citizenship, not a separate State citizenship.
Section 9 of the Act: an Indian who voluntarily takes another country's citizenship stops being an Indian citizen.
So A is true and R explains it.
PYQ-POL-APK-A8689A.also: OCI (Overseas Citizen of India) card, added in 2005, is not dual citizenship; it gives no voting right.

PYQ-POL-APK-AF5BFE.lead: Article 51A(g): protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, wildlife.
points: Article 48A is a duty of the State, not of citizens.
Both 51A and 48A were added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.

PYQ-POL-APK-B531D5.lead: The RTI Act, 2005 requires a reply to information requests within 30 days.
points: The Public Information Officer must reply within 30 days; within 48 hours if life or liberty is involved.
The e-governance plan and Aadhaar are service delivery and identity schemes; they set no legal time limit for information.
The Right to Education Act, 2009 gives free schooling to children aged 6-14.
PYQ-POL-APK-B531D5.also: RTI Act came fully into force on 12 October 2005.

PYQ-POL-APK-C0BE25.lead: Sections 3 to 6: birth, descent, registration, naturalisation — in that order.
points: This gives A-4, B-3, C-2, D-1, which is option 2.
PYQ-POL-APK-C0BE25.also: Section 7 covers the fifth mode: incorporation of territory.

PYQ-POL-APK-DBE422.lead: Article 39A (equal justice, free legal aid) was added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.
points: Both statements are correct, so option 3.
PYQ-POL-APK-DBE422.also: The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 gives effect to Article 39A.

PYQ-POL-APK-DFBFA1.lead: Act passed in 1955; single citizenship means one citizenship for all.
points: This gives A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2, which is option 2.

PYQ-POL-APK-E576EB.lead: NRI holds an Indian passport abroad; OCI is a registered cardholder.

Meaning

Self or ancestor was an Indian national
Registered OCI cardholder under the Act

points: This gives A-3, B-4, C-2, D-1, which is option 3.
The PIO card scheme was merged into OCI in 2015.

PYQ-POL-APK-E7968C.lead: Article 84: minimum age 30 for Rajya Sabha, 25 for Lok Sabha.
points: Article 84(b) sets 30 years for Rajya Sabha and 25 years for Lok Sabha.
35 is the minimum age for President and Vice-President.
PYQ-POL-APK-E7968C.also: State Legislative Council member: 30 years; Assembly member: 25 years.

PYQ-POL-APK-FC0A3B.lead: The Act gives five modes: birth, descent, registration, naturalisation, incorporation of territory.
points: Sections 3 to 7 cover these five modes one by one.
Loss of citizenship has three ways: renunciation, termination and deprivation (Sections 8-10).

PYQ-POL-D5A5E43E1BCA.lead: Adoption is not a mode of acquiring citizenship under the 1955 Act.
points: The five modes are birth, descent, registration, naturalisation and incorporation of territory.
Registration, birth and descent are all valid modes.
A minor child of Indian citizens may be registered under Section 5(1)(d), but adoption alone gives nothing.

PYQ-POL-E4541AA4B129.lead: Citizenship is in Part II of the Constitution, Articles 5 to 11.
points: Articles 2-4 (Part I) deal with new States and changing State boundaries.
Articles 15-21 and 25-31 are Fundamental Rights in Part III.
Article 31 (property) was repealed by the 44th Amendment, 1978.

PYQ-POL-F52BE1C5C794.lead: Article 11 gives Parliament the power to regulate citizenship by law.
points: Parliament used this power to pass the Citizenship Act, 1955.
The Union Cabinet administers laws; the Supreme Court interprets them; the Law Commission only advises.
PYQ-POL-F52BE1C5C794.also: Citizenship is Entry 17 of the Union List.

points: Under Article 5, a person domiciled in India needed birth in India, a parent born in India, or 5 years' residence.

PYQ-POL-WEB-10C92F.lead: Articles 15, 16, 19, 29 and 30 are for citizens only.
points: I, II and IV are correct, so option 2.
PYQ-POL-WEB-10C92F.also: Article 15 (no discrimination) is also for citizens only.

PYQ-POL-WEB-1FBC78.lead: Article 19's six freedoms are given only to citizens.
points: Article 20 (protection in conviction), 21 (life and liberty) and 22 (arrest safeguards) apply to all persons, including foreigners.

PYQ-POL-WEB-25A1D0.lead: Protecting weaker sections is a Directive Principle (Article 46), not a Fundamental Duty.
points: II, III and IV are correct, so option 3.

PYQ-POL-WEB-3BD101.lead: Only statement 1 is right; US has dual citizenship, and naturalised citizens can be deprived.
points: Only statement 1 is correct, so option 4.

PYQ-POL-WEB-463F9E.lead: Rights are claims of citizens that the State must respect.
points: Rights limit the State's power over individuals, not the other way round.
Rights are not mere privileges; and they belong to all, not to a few.

PYQ-POL-WEB-508FE4.lead: No duty requires 5 years of compulsory national service.
points: Article 51A(d) only asks citizens to defend the country and render national service when called upon.
Option 1 is 51A(b), option 3 is 51A(h), option 4 is 51A(i).
PYQ-POL-WEB-508FE4.also: There are 11 Fundamental Duties; the 11th (education of children 6-14) was added by the 86th Amendment, 2002.

PYQ-POL-WEB-5403C1.lead: Six Fundamental Rights remain after the right to property was removed.
points: The six: Equality, Freedom, against Exploitation, Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational, Constitutional Remedies.
Originally there were seven; the 44th Amendment, 1978 removed the right to property.
PYQ-POL-WEB-5403C1.also: Property is now a legal right under Article 300A.

PYQ-POL-WEB-65CAB0.lead: 51A(a): abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals, institutions, National Flag and Anthem.
points: Secularism, socialism and democracy are values in the Preamble, not words of 51A(a).

PYQ-POL-WEB-713319.lead: Article 19 freedoms, including trade and profession, are only for Indian citizens.
points: Freedom of trade and profession is Article 19(1)(g), so a foreigner cannot claim it.
Equality before law (Art 14), life and liberty (Art 21) and freedom of religion (Art 25) apply to all persons.

PYQ-POL-WEB-72D776.lead: The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended Fundamental Duties.
points: The 42nd Amendment, 1976 added them as Part IV-A, Article 51A.
Raja Chelliah worked on tax reform; Santhanam on corruption (led to CVC); Kelkar on tax and fiscal reform.
PYQ-POL-WEB-72D776.also: The committee suggested 8 duties; the 42nd Amendment added 10.

PYQ-POL-WEB-8D20EB.lead: In the US, a person is a citizen of the country and of their State.
points: This dual citizenship is within one federation, not two countries.
India has single citizenship; there is no separate State citizenship.

PYQ-POL-WEB-9399C6.lead: Article 15 bars discrimination on religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

PYQ-POL-WEB-99CCFB.lead: The State can make laws regulating religion; the right is not absolute.
points: Article 25(2) lets the State regulate secular activities linked with religion and make social reform laws.
Options 1, 2 and 3 are true: Articles 25(1) and 26 give these freedoms, subject to public order, morality and health.
Article 25 is available to all persons, not only citizens.

PYQ-POL-WEB-A4107D.lead: Right to property was removed from Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment, 1978.

PYQ-POL-WEB-B9481C.lead: Scientific temper is a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(h).
points: Articles 49A, 50A and 52A do not exist in the Constitution.
Article 51A, Part IV-A, lists all Fundamental Duties.

PYQ-POL-WEB-BE0200.lead: Citizenship is in Part II, Articles 5 to 11.
points: Articles 12 onward begin Part III (Fundamental Rights).
The other ranges mix citizenship and Fundamental Rights articles.

PYQ-POL-WEB-C93876.lead: The President is the first citizen, being head of the State.
points: Article 52: there shall be a President of India; executive power vests in him (Art 53).
The President is first in the Order of Precedence; the Prime Minister is third, after the Vice-President.

PYQ-POL-WEB-CB1FCB.lead: Parliament passed the Citizenship Act in 1955.
points: 1950 is when the Constitution (Articles 5-11) came into force.
The Act has been amended in 1957, 1986, 1992, 2003, 2005, 2015 and 2019.

PYQ-POL-WEB-D3110F.lead: Article 11 gives Parliament full power to make citizenship laws.

PYQ-POL-WEB-D5CD8D.lead: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949.
points: 26 January 1950 is when it came fully into force.
26 November is now observed as Constitution Day (since 2015).
PYQ-POL-WEB-D5CD8D.also: Some provisions like citizenship and elections came into force on 26 November 1949 itself.

points: Options 2, 3 and 4 each drop one word, so they are incomplete.
PYQ-POL-WEB-E49E33.also: The Preamble promises Justice (social, economic, political), Liberty, Equality and Fraternity.
